analysis.brief_en: Japan-based Takeda Biopharmaceuticals announced on 20 July 2026 that India’s Drug Controller General (DCGI) has granted approval for QDENGA, the country’s first dengue vaccine. The live-attenuated, tetravalent vaccine targets all four dengue serotypes and is authorized for individuals aged 4–60 without prior infection screening, simplifying delivery in routine care. Clinical data from over 28,000 participants across 19 trials show 80.2% efficacy against laboratory-confirmed dengue one year after the two-dose schedule, with 90.4% protection against hospitalizations after 18 months and sustained benefit up to seven years. WHO has prequalified QDENGA and recommends it for dengue-endemic settings, supporting broader public health use. India recorded more than 113,000 dengue cases in 2025, though modeling suggests the true burden is far higher. Takeda now plans to collaborate with Indian regulators and health stakeholders to scale access as part of the national dengue prevention strategy.
